# BPCS Interlock Definition Sheet: Template and Worked Example

## How this handles your three goals

| Goal | How the template handles it |
|---|---|
| **(a) Configurer can implement from it** | Each sheet defines causes, logic, effects, latching, reset, bypass, bad-quality handling and controller interactions. These are the items usually missing from old C&E drawings. |
| **(b) FAT can write a test step straight from it** | Section 10 is a test matrix. Each row points back to a numbered section of the sheet, so the tester knows which requirement they are checking. |
| **(c) Setpoints in one place only** | The sheet never holds a setpoint value. It holds a **Setpoint ID** that points to a single **Trip & Alarm Setpoint Register**. The register is the only controlled source of values. See the rules below. |

### Setpoint single-source rules

1. **The register is the only source.** All trip, alarm and permissive values, delays and hysteresis live in one Trip & Alarm Setpoint Register. Each entry has: Setpoint ID, tag, value, units, basis, revision and approver. Keep it in the instrument database (SPI, Smart Instrumentation or similar) or a controlled spreadsheet.
2. **Other documents use the ID only.** Interlock sheets, C&E charts, FAT procedures, operating procedures and HMI specs all write the Setpoint ID, for example `SP-1105-LT`, never "1.2 barg".
3. **DCS configuration is checked against the register.** At FAT, export the configured values from the new DCS and compare them automatically to the register at a stated revision. This is one test step for the whole unit, not one per interlock.
4. **Test records note the value used.** The tester writes down the value they applied and the register revision. That is evidence of what was tested, not a second source.
5. **Changing a value is a register change only.** It goes through MOC against the register. No other document needs revising.

**Practical tip:** with about 40 units, keep these sheets as structured data rather than Word documents. One row per cause, effect and test case in a database or a controlled workbook lets you generate the C&E matrix, FAT procedures and a register cross-check automatically. The template below maps onto that structure directly.

---

## Template: BPCS Interlock Definition Sheet

### 0. Header

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Interlock ID | `IL-<unit>-<nnn>` |
| Title | |
| Unit / Area | |
| Revision / Date / Status | Draft / IFR / IFC / As-built |
| Function type | Process trip / Permissive / Equipment protection / Sequence interlock |
| Hazard study reference | HAZOP node / scenario no. |
| LOPA credit claimed? | No / Yes. If yes: IPL ID, PFD claimed, and confirmation that this function is independent of the initiating cause and of other BPCS layers. |
| Related SIS function (not documented here) | SIF ID in the SRS, or "None" |
| P&ID(s) | |
| Legacy reference | Old DCS logic sheet / C&E drawing / point names |
| Owner (process / control engineer) | |

### 1. Purpose

One or two sentences: what hazard or equipment damage this prevents, and what "safe state" means.

### 2. Causes (initiators)

| # | Tag | Description | I/O type & range | Condition | Setpoint ID | Delay ID | Hysteresis / Reset ID | Voting | Bad-quality action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | | | AI 4–20 mA, x–y units | PV < SP / PV > SP / DI = state | `SP-…` | `TD-…` or "none" | `HY-…` | 1oo1 / 2oo3 … | Treat as tripped / Alarm only / Hold last |

**Bad-quality action** covers open circuit, out of range and communication loss. Write the reason for the choice in Section 8.

### 3. Logic

- **Plain-language statement:** "If C1 OR C2 for longer than delay, then E1 and E2."
- **Boolean expression:** `TRIP = (C1 AND NOT BYP1) OR C2`
- **Latching:** Latched until reset / Non-latching
- **First-out:** Yes / No. Which causes are included in the first-out group?
- **Logic diagram reference:** functional logic diagram number, if one is produced.

### 4. Effects (final actions)

| # | Tag | Description | Action on trip | Fail-safe position (air / signal loss) | Position feedback | Discrepancy action & timer ID | Released for operator control after reset? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | | | Close / Open / Stop / Force output to x% / Force to MAN | FC / FO / FL | ZSC / ZSO tags | Alarm `DA-…` after `TD-…` | Requires separate operator command / Auto |

### 5. Interactions with control loops and other logic

- Controllers forced to Manual, Tracking or a fixed output on trip, and their anti-windup behaviour.
- Other interlocks this one initiates, or is initiated by.
- Sequences affected (start-up, light-off, shutdown).

### 6. Reset and restart

- **Reset conditions:** for example, all causes healthy AND all effects confirmed in safe state.
- **Reset location and authority:** operator HMI / field pushbutton / supervisor.
- **After reset:** effects stay in safe state until an operator command, or they release automatically. State which.

### 7. Bypass, override and start-up inhibit

| Item | Entry |
|---|---|
| Maintenance bypass allowed? | Yes / No |
| Bypass method & authority | HMI with key / permit level |
| Bypass indication & alarm | |
| Max bypass duration / auto-removal | `TD-…` |
| Automatic start-up inhibit | Condition, timer ID, and how it is removed |
| Procedure / MOC reference | |

### 8. Fault handling and design decisions

Record bad-quality handling, controller or IO card failure behaviour, and power-up state. Give the reason for each choice, for example "spurious trip judged acceptable vs. loss of protection".

### 9. HMI and alarms

| Alarm / Indication | Tag / Alarm ID | Priority (from alarm database) | Display |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pre-alarm | | | |
| Trip | | | |
| First-out | | | |
| Bypass active | | | |
| Valve discrepancy | | | |

### 10. Test matrix (FAT / SAT)

| TC | Verifies § | Initial conditions | Action | Expected result | Pass/Fail | Value applied & register rev |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TC1 | 2, 3, 4 | | | | | |

Minimum test cases for every interlock:

1. Trip at setpoint.
2. No trip just inside setpoint.
3. Delay timing.
4. Bad quality on each cause.
5. Latching holds when the cause clears.
6. Reset blocked while a cause is present.
7. Reset succeeds when causes are healthy.
8. Effects do not release unexpectedly after reset.
9. Bypass works, alarms, and times out.
10. Start-up inhibit works and expires.
11. Controller interactions occur as specified.
12. Alarms and first-out appear as specified.

### 11. Migration notes

- Behaviour in the legacy system, including any undocumented behaviour found in the logic.
- Deliberate deviations from legacy behaviour, each with its reason and MOC reference.
- Open questions, each with an owner.

### 12. Approval

Process, Control/Instrument, Operations, and Safety (if LOPA credit is claimed). Name, signature and date for each.

## Worked Example: IL-11-004, Heater H-1101 Low Fuel Gas Pressure

**Assumptions to verify for your site.** These are marked ⚠ below.

- In many refineries, low burner fuel gas pressure is handled in the BMS/SIS (API 556, NFPA 85/86 practice). This example assumes the SIS or BMS has its own separate low-low trip, and this BPCS interlock is an earlier, operational layer.
- If anyone takes LOPA credit for this BPCS function, it needs the extra rigour noted in the header.
- PT-1105 is assumed to be downstream of XV-1106. That placement is why the start-up inhibit in Section 7 is needed.

### 0. Header

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Interlock ID | IL-11-004 |
| Title | H-1101 low main burner fuel gas pressure, close main fuel valve |
| Unit / Area | Unit 11 / Heater H-1101 |
| Revision / Status | Rev A / Draft for review |
| Function type | Process trip |
| Hazard study reference | HAZOP U11 Node 7, Scenario 7.3 (low fuel pressure causing flame instability and loss of flame) ⚠ |
| LOPA credit claimed? | **No** ⚠ (confirm against the LOPA) |
| Related SIS function | SIF-11-002, low-low fuel gas pressure via PT-1105B ⚠ (documented in the SRS, not here) |
| P&ID(s) | 11-PID-0042 ⚠ |
| Legacy reference | Old DCS logic sheet L-11-17; C&E drawing 11-CE-003 row 4 ⚠ |

### 1. Purpose

Low main burner fuel gas pressure can cause flame instability or flameout, followed by fuel accumulating in the firebox. This interlock closes the main fuel gas shutoff valve XV-1106 before pressure reaches the SIS low-low trip point. **Safe state:** XV-1106 closed and TIC-1101 in Manual at minimum output. Pilots are not affected.

### 2. Causes

| # | Tag | Description | I/O & range | Condition | Setpoint ID | Delay ID | Hysteresis ID | Voting | Bad-quality action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | PT-1105 | Main burner fuel gas pressure, downstream of XV-1106 | AI 4–20 mA HART, 0–X barg | PV < SP | `SP-1105-LT` | `TD-1105-LT` | `HY-1105-LT` | 1oo1 | **Treat as tripped** (see §8) ⚠ |

### 3. Logic

- **Plain-language statement:** If PT-1105 is below the low trip setpoint for longer than the trip delay, and the start-up inhibit is not active, close XV-1106 and force TIC-1101 to Manual at minimum output.
- **Boolean expression:** `TRIP = (C1_LOW_DLY OR C1_BADQ) AND NOT SU_INHIBIT AND NOT MAINT_BYP`
- **Latching:** Latched until reset.
- **First-out:** Yes. Part of the H-1101 heater first-out group, together with IL-11-001 to IL-11-006.

### 4. Effects

| # | Tag | Description | Action on trip | Fail-safe | Feedback | Discrepancy | After reset |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | XV-1106 | Main fuel gas shutoff valve | De-energise solenoid (close) | Fail closed | ZSC-1106, ZSO-1106 | Alarm `DA-1106` if ZSC is not made within `TD-1106-TRV` | Stays closed until operator OPEN command |
| E2 | TIC-1101 | Heater outlet temperature controller (cascade to fuel PIC) | Force to MAN, output to light-off position `SP-1101-LO` | n/a | n/a | n/a | Stays in MAN. Operator returns it to AUTO. |

### 5. Interactions

- The fuel gas pressure controller in cascade under TIC-1101 goes into tracking while E2 is active, to prevent windup.
- This interlock does not trip pilots or the heater feed. Feed protection is covered by IL-11-002.
- The light-off sequence uses the start-up inhibit in Section 7.

### 6. Reset and restart

- **Reset conditions:** ZSC-1106 made, AND TIC-1101 output at or below the light-off position. The PT-1105 condition is excluded from the reset conditions, because pressure is zero while XV-1106 is closed. Protection on restart comes from the start-up inhibit in Section 7.
- **Reset location and authority:** Console operator, from the H-1101 overview faceplate.
- **After reset:** XV-1106 stays closed until the operator issues an OPEN command, and only if the BMS permissives are healthy.

### 7. Bypass and start-up inhibit

| Item | Entry |
|---|---|
| Maintenance bypass | Allowed, for transmitter maintenance only. Supervisor-level HMI key. |
| Bypass indication | `BYP-IL-11-004` alarm and banner on the heater overview |
| Max bypass duration | `TD-IL-11-004-BYP`, then automatic removal with an alarm |
| Start-up inhibit | Starts automatically on the XV-1106 OPEN command. Duration `TD-1105-SU`. Ends early if PV exceeds `SP-1105-LT` + `HY-1105-LT`. Cannot be extended or re-armed while XV-1106 is open. |
| Procedure reference | OP-11-H1101-02 (light-off) ⚠ |

### 8. Fault handling and design decisions

- **PT-1105 bad quality → trip.** Unnoticed loss of low-pressure protection was judged worse than a spurious fuel trip, given that pilots remain lit ⚠. This must be confirmed with Operations at the interlock review.
- **Controller failover:** the interlock state is retained.
- **IO card failure:** the output de-energises, so XV-1106 closes.
- **Cold start / power-up:** the interlock starts in the tripped state and needs a reset.
- **Legacy deviation:** the old system did not trip on bad quality. See Section 11.

### 9. HMI and alarms

| Item | Alarm ID | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| PT-1105 low pre-alarm | `PAL-1105` (setpoint `SP-1105-L`) | From alarm database |
| Interlock tripped | `IL-11-004-TRIP` | From alarm database |
| First-out | H-1101 first-out group | n/a |
| Bypass active | `BYP-IL-11-004` | From alarm database |
| XV-1106 discrepancy | `DA-1106` | From alarm database |

### 10. Test matrix

Setpoint values are taken from the Trip & Alarm Setpoint Register at the revision stated on the test record.

| TC | Verifies § | Initial conditions | Action | Expected result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TC1 | 2, 3, 4 | Heater simulated firing, XV-1106 open, TIC-1101 AUTO, inhibit expired | Ramp PT-1105 to just below `SP-1105-LT` | After `TD-1105-LT`: XV-1106 commanded closed, TIC-1101 MAN at `SP-1101-LO`, trip alarm and first-out shown |
| TC2 | 2 | As TC1 | Hold PT-1105 just above `SP-1105-LT` | No trip. `PAL-1105` active if below `SP-1105-L`. |
| TC3 | 2 | As TC1 | Drop PT-1105 below SP, then restore before `TD-1105-LT` expires | No trip |
| TC4 | 2, 8 | As TC1 | Force PT-1105 bad quality (open circuit / >20.5 mA) | Immediate trip, bad-quality alarm |
| TC5 | 3 | Tripped | Restore PT-1105 to normal | Interlock stays latched, XV-1106 stays closed |
| TC6 | 6 | Tripped, ZSC-1106 simulated not made | Attempt reset | Reset rejected, message shown |
| TC7 | 6 | Tripped, ZSC made, TIC-1101 output at light-off | Reset | Reset accepted, XV-1106 remains closed |
| TC8 | 7 | Reset, PT-1105 = 0 | Operator OPEN XV-1106 | Inhibit starts. No trip during `TD-1105-SU`. Trip occurs at expiry if PV is still low. |
| TC9 | 7 | As TC8 | Raise PV above `SP-1105-LT` + `HY-1105-LT` during inhibit | Inhibit ends early. A later low PV trips. |
| TC10 | 7 | Running | Apply maintenance bypass with supervisor key; drop PV low | No trip. Bypass alarm and banner shown. Bypass auto-removes after `TD-IL-11-004-BYP`. |
| TC11 | 4 | Trip active | Simulate ZSC-1106 failing to make | `DA-1106` after `TD-1106-TRV` |
| TC12 | 5 | Trip active | Observe fuel PIC | PIC in tracking, no windup on return to AUTO |

### 11. Migration notes

- **Legacy behaviour:** the old system had no bad-quality trip. The start-up inhibit was a fixed timer in a separate logic block (sheet L-11-19). The setpoint was hard-coded in that block, and it differed from C&E 11-CE-003 ⚠. Resolve this against the register before FAT.
- **Deviations:** adding the bad-quality trip and the discrepancy alarm requires an MOC (ref. TBD).
- **Open items:** confirm the PT-1105 location relative to XV-1106 on site (owner: Instrument Eng.). Confirm that no LOPA credit is claimed (owner: Process Safety).

### Matching register entries (the only place values appear)

| Setpoint ID | Tag | Function | Value | Units | Basis | Rev |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP-1105-L | PT-1105 | Low pre-alarm | *tbd* | barg | Burner vendor data | A |
| SP-1105-LT | PT-1105 | Low trip (BPCS) | *tbd* | barg | Burner stability limit, margin above SIS LL | A |
| HY-1105-LT | PT-1105 | Trip reset hysteresis | *tbd* | barg | | A |
| TD-1105-LT | PT-1105 | Trip delay | *tbd* | s | Noise / transient filtering | A |
| TD-1105-SU | PT-1105 | Start-up inhibit | *tbd* | s | Measured pressurisation time | A |
| TD-1106-TRV | XV-1106 | Travel / discrepancy | *tbd* | s | Valve stroke time + margin | A |
| SP-1101-LO | TIC-1101 | Light-off output | *tbd* | % | Burner vendor data | A |

---

## Before rolling this out

Hold a short interlock review per unit with Operations before configuration starts. The sections that most often expose problems in legacy logic are 6 (reset), 7 (bypass and start-up inhibit) and 8 (bad quality). Settling them on paper is much cheaper than finding them at FAT or during commissioning.
